processNote: Three learnings this issue produced, sent to the implementer for the retro so they reach docs/solutions/ rather than staying in Envoy. One: a number changed in one place is a search of the file, not a read of the section being edited — the resource table sat seventy lines above the paragraph three roles argued about across three rounds, and nobody opened it. Two, the reviewer's own: a reviewer who agrees with a passage's conclusion stops checking its reasoning, which is how a comment with the Kubernetes ordering backwards was endorsed as correct in a round-2 review body and survived into the next round; an endorsement is a claim in the same evidence bracket as the rest. Three: a decision taken between rounds lives only in Envoy, and a relaunched pane loses Envoy — the architect's deletion decision reached the implementer twice and arrived neither time. Both practice changes attach to the roles that made them: the reviewer records a between-rounds decision in the review body and in this file; the implementer asks the owning role which is current when a recreated pane meets a disagreement.
